answer: Sybil resistance can rest on spot audits rather than identity checks. Each epoch the protocol commits a seed, then draws a random sample of submissions - this round, three tasks labelled shale, mesa and sparrow - and routes each to verifiers who did not originally grade it, paying only when their verdict matches the majority. Since that seed is fixed before answers arrive, an operator with ten thousand keys cannot tell which will be rechecked. Detection probability stays flat per submission, so expected slashing grows linearly with the number of fakes; no volume discount exists.
